messages:
julian: Heads-up — we need to revoke log access for a contractor immediately after yesterday's incident. They still have S3/SIEM read and some console sessions. What's the fastest safe path to lock them down?

sara: Do we mean Splunk/SIEM read tokens, S3 archived logs, or KMS-wrapped artifacts?

julian: All of the above. Contractor account `contractor123` had `se_support` role with S3Read + splunk-reader. They were used for triage.

anika: Priority list: 1) disable credentials/sessions, 2) stop any live export/forwarding pipelines, 3) rewrap or rotate keys for sensitive objects, 4) capture audit evidence.

mike: Quick practical: delete their access keys, block console, and remove from groups. Commands (run from a secure admin session):
```bash
# list + delete access keys
aws iam list-access-keys --user-name contractor123
aws iam delete-access-key --user-name contractor123 --access-key-id AKIA...
# force console lock
aws iam update-login-profile --user-name contractor123 --password-reset-required
# remove from support group
aws iam remove-user-from-group --user-name contractor123 --group-name se-support
```

anika: For active role sessions we don't have a single revoke API across all STS tokens. Short-term workaround: attach a deny policy that matches the principal or change the role trust policy to disallow assumption. Also create an explicit deny for `s3:*` + `kms:Decrypt` scoped to that principal.

security-oncall: Quick action checklist (I ran through):
- Disabled user console + deleted access keys (mike)
- Stopped Splunk HEC token used by the pipeline
- Paused Kinesis -> SIEM connectors
- Created evidence bucket `sec-evidence/INC-452` (restricted ACL)

security-oncall: Splunk HEC disable steps we used:
```text
1) In Splunk UI: Settings -> Data Inputs -> HTTP Event Collector -> find token -> Disable
2) Rotate any authtokens for onboarded forwarders
```

aaron: I can handle KMS wrap/rewrap. Suggestion: do not rotate the CMK unless absolutely necessary because CMK rotation has broader blast radius. Instead, generate a new data key and re-encrypt affected objects and replace the SSE-KMS key on the object copies. I'll schedule a timeboxed rewrap job.

mike: For S3 re-encryption quick pattern: copy objects to a staging prefix with `--sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id new-key`, verify checksums, and atomically swap prefixes. Keep originals until retention/forensics team signs off.

julian: Who has permissions to run the rewrap job? Need someone with kms:Encrypt, s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject. @aaron?

aaron: Yup I have the perms. I'll run in a dedicated admin account and log the steps.

sara: We'll need audit entries for compliance: record `iam.delete-access-key`, `iam.update-login-profile`, `kms:ReEncrypt`, `s3:PutObject` in core-audit. Please include request IDs and snapshot of principals. Also flag in case we need to subpoena chain-of-custody.

julian: For SIEM exports: Mike, can you confirm all external forwarders are disabled and that we stop any delivery to external consumers? We don't want a live export continuing.

mike: Confirmed — I disabled the HEC token and paused the Kinesis Firehose stream to the external tenant. Command I ran: `aws firehose stop-delivery-stream --delivery-stream-name sec-firehose-to-splunk` (then verified in Splunk UI).

anika: Ops/process note: update the oncall playbook with an explicit "revoke-forwarding" step under containment. Right now it's implicit and folks miss it. I'll open a PR to add the checklist.

devops-bot: INCIDENT-452 created, assigned to @julian, severity P2. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/incident-452

julian: Also proposal: we should move to stricter ephemeral access for 3rd parties — default deny plus JIT access for investigations. Use short-lived STS assume-role durations (900s) and require re-auth for longer jobs.

mike: Agreed. Practical pattern: centralize 3rd-party roles under `thirdparty/investigation` with no standing access; use `aws sts assume-role --duration-seconds 900` for jump sessions. That reduces blast radius.

anika: One more compliance question — retention on the security S3 bucket currently 365 days. For this incident we need artifacts for forensic review for 540 days. We should file retention exception if we extend. @sara can you start that?

sara: Filing retention exception now and tagging it to INC-452. Also copying legal/compliance.

julian: I'll open the PR to update the runbook and include the exact commands we used plus fields to record in the audit entry.

anika: Let's also schedule a tabletop to walk through revocation + rewrap next week. If we can make the runbook less ad-hoc, we'll be faster next time.

julian: Next steps summary: @aaron — rewrap/encrypt affected objects (timeboxed); @mike — confirm SIEM exports remain stopped & rotate tokens; @sara — file retention/exemption & audit ticket; @anika — update runbook PR; @julian — PR + coordinate tabletop.

sara: will do. Target completion EOD tomorrow for containment tasks.

aaron: starting rewrap job in 15m in staging, will post logs to `sec-evidence/INC-452/logs.txt`.

julian: thanks everyone. Please paste any command output into the evidence bucket and do not share results publicly. :eyes:
